description: Evergreen conifer. Needles borne in fascicles, persisting several years. Reproduction by woody seed cones; there are NO flowers, no petals and no fruit of any kind.
source: Flora of North America vol. 2 (Pinaceae); card #41
notes: A conifer has no flowers. Any requirement for petals or fruit is botanically wrong for this species and must never be inferred from a colour signature -- sunlit needles against sky previously registered as 'white flowers'. Cones are welcome but are absent for much of the year. FRAMING: card #41 shows a BRANCH with needles at close range, not a whole tree. A habit shot of an entire pine is correct botany and the wrong scale -- at 593px wide the needles become canopy texture. Prefer a branch or shoot. IDENTITY: 'a conifer' is not an identification. Needle fascicle count is the field character and the vision pass should report it when resolvable.
derived_from: botanical description and the printed card, NOT a colour signature

framing.prefer: a branch or shoot at close range, needles individually resolvable
framing.avoid: a whole-tree habit shot; at 593px the needles become canopy texture
framing.reference: card #41, which shows a branch with needle fascicles and a cone

identity_check: Pinus strobus has needles in fascicles of FIVE, soft and slender. Most other eastern pines carry two or three. A candidate must be confirmed as this species, not merely as 'a pine' -- the observation taxon is re-checked at retrieval and the vision pass is asked to confirm the fascicle count where it is visible.
